I was born and raised in a small town nestled in the rolling hills of Vermont. My parents were both teachers and instilled in me a deep love for learning from an early age. Growing up, I spent hours reading books, exploring the woods behind our house, and tinkering with various projects in our garage. I had a particular fascination with language and would often spend afternoons writing short stories and poetry.

As I grew older, my interests began to expand beyond my hometown. I developed a passion for travel and adventure, seeking out new experiences and cultures wherever I went. In high school, I participated in several exchange programs, living with host families in France, Spain, and Japan. These experiences opened my eyes to the vast diversity of the world and solidified my desire to continue exploring it.

After graduating from high school, I attended a small liberal arts college in New England, where I studied linguistics and anthropology. During my time in college, I became increasingly interested in the ways that language shapes our perceptions of the world and how we interact with one another. I also had the opportunity to participate in several study abroad programs, including a semester in Morocco and a summer in Brazil.

Following graduation, I moved to New York City to pursue a career in publishing. I worked as an editorial assistant at a small press, where I learned the ins and outs of the industry. However, I soon realized that my true passion lay in working directly with language and its impact on individuals and communities. I decided to go back to school to earn a master's degree in speech-language pathology.

Throughout my graduate studies, I specialized in bilingual language development and disorders. I worked with diverse populations, including refugees and immigrants, and saw firsthand the challenges they faced in navigating complex linguistic systems. This experience further solidified my belief in the importance of promoting access to language and communication for all individuals.

After earning my master's degree, I returned to New York City and began working as a speech-language pathologist in a public school. In this role, I have been able to help students overcome language barriers and develop their communication skills. I have also had the opportunity to collaborate with teachers and administrators to create inclusive classroom environments that support linguistic diversity.

Outside of my professional life, I continue to be an avid reader and writer. I regularly attend literary events and workshops, and I have published several pieces of creative nonfiction in local journals. I also enjoy hiking, cooking, and practicing yoga. Recently, I have taken up photography as a way to capture the beauty of the world around me.

In the coming years, I plan to continue working as a speech-language pathologist while also pursuing opportunities to advocate for linguistic rights and access. I believe that everyone deserves the chance to communicate freely and express themselves in their own unique voice, and I am dedicated to helping make that vision a reality.
